sections.html: Goodeids are livebearing fishes. Skiffia multipunctata reach a maximum size of about 6 cm, and males always stay smaller than the females. The males vary a lot in coloration.
Goodeids are kept best in unheated aquaria. During the warm season the fish are particularly suitable for outdoor aquaria.
In the wild Skiffia feed a lot on algae. In aquaria they readily take any usual fish food, but a good flake food has proved to be the best for the species.
Males always stay smaller than the females. The males vary a lot regarding coloration.
Lexicon: Skiffia: dedication name for F. J. V. Skiff, a former director of the Field Columbian Museum in Chicago. multipunctata: Latin, means "with many spots".
